fallback.heading: Unmapped status
fallback.summary: Cargo state is not mapped in this assistant version. Manually review the record, documents, and negotiations.
fallback.explanation: I could not identify this stage precisely yet. I will support you with a safe fallback guidance so you can keep moving with context.
nextSteps: Validate status with the operations team.
Check documentation and upcoming milestones on the cargo view.
risks: Automated interpretation is limited — confirm with an official source.

open.heading: Open status
open.summary: Cargo posted on the marketplace; awaiting proposals aligned with route, type, and stated constraints.
open.explanation: There is no confirmed transport commitment yet. The best move now is to attract compatible proposals and keep key information ready for a faster decision.
nextSteps: Review the suggested document package and gaps before the first booking.
Monitor the operating window and interest signals along the corridor.
Record clarifications on the record if the operation requires additional conditions.
risks: Proposals incompatible with draft, temperature, or timing may delay logistics fit.
Low connectivity at origin may delay how the market perceives status updates.

bidding.heading: Bidding status
bidding.summary: Quotes or counteroffers are under review; the decision rests with the shipper and involved parties.
bidding.explanation: Your cargo is already in negotiation. This is the right moment to compare options carefully and balance price, timing, and documentary safety.
nextSteps: Compare terms, amounts, and document commitments in each proposal.
Request formal adjustments when evidence or an operational clause is missing.
Set an internal deadline to accept or decline so the window is not missed.
risks: Stalling in the bidding phase may expire the planned loading window.
Ambiguity in tax or sanitary paperwork can reopen negotiation.

contracting.heading: Contracting status
contracting.summary: Negotiation moved to contracting; focus on formalization, documents, and capacity booking.
contracting.explanation: You are close to closing. Focus now on final contractual and operational checks to proceed with confidence.
nextSteps: Validate drafts, guarantees, and responsibilities before final acceptance.
Align loading with real berth and draft availability.
Plan the loading checklist and evidence required by the route.
risks: Contract rollback if regulatory requirements are not met in time.
Third-party dependencies (terminal, inspections) may extend timelines.

reserved.heading: Reserved status
reserved.summary: Your cargo is already reserved. Now it is worth aligning the final details so boarding can move forward more safely.
reserved.explanation: The operation already has a confirmed reservation. To keep things moving without delays, it is worth closing the final pending items for this stage.
nextSteps: Confirm seals, temperature, and lots with the carrier.
This is a good time to complete the required documents.
After that, schedule the docking window and pier check.
risks: There are still document adjustments that may delay cargo release if they are not resolved on time.
River or port conditions may require small planning adjustments.
The cold-chain window is short and deserves extra attention.
Signal between smaller terminals may vary and reduce tracking predictability.

boarded.heading: Loaded / in-transit status
boarded.summary: Cargo loaded or on inland waterway transit; monitor events, synchronization, and operational proof.
boarded.explanation: The operation is in motion. The priority now is route visibility, quick incident response, and clear communication with stakeholders.
nextSteps: Follow tracking and incident logs along the corridor.
Keep a contingency channel for delays or route deviations.
Prepare POD validation and fiscal closing.
risks: Segments with limited signal may delay near–real-time visibility.
Seasonal variation can affect ETA and cabotage connections.

delivered.heading: Delivered status
delivered.summary: Main flow completed in the simulated operational view; focus on proof and closure.
delivered.explanation: Main delivery is complete. The next step is to finalize documents, capture lessons learned, and close the operation safely.
nextSteps: Archive proof of delivery, receipts, and relevant communications.
Capture lessons learned and metrics for future cycles.
Validate document discharge and billing per contract.
risks: Post-delivery issues (volume mismatch, damage) may appear after unloading.
Incomplete document retention can affect future audits.

meaning.cost: This indicator shows how consolidating cargoes and improving route predictability can reduce friction and operational cost over time.
meaning.sustainability: This indicator describes the potential for lower emissions when water transport replaces long road segments, varying by route and operation.
meaning.regional: This indicator contextualizes the relevance of navigable waterways in the North, where rivers are core logistics infrastructure.
meaning.automation: This indicator summarizes how standardizing terms, documents, and history helps reduce rework and delays before shipment.
meaning.brdomar: This indicator connects the product to Brazil’s cabotage institutional context (BR do Mar), without claiming official participation.
meaning.compliance: This indicator shows how organizing tax, environmental, and sanitary requirements reduces contracting risk and improves auditability.
meaning.connectivity: This indicator explains why capturing events and evidence under low connectivity supports operational traceability.
meaning.government: This indicator shows how territorial reading and aggregated indicators can support institutional coordination and decisions.

cost: Improves comparison of proposals and an auditable pricing trail.
Reduces empty backhauls by aligning routes and utilization.
Increases predictability and reduces operational rework.
sustainability: Helps prioritize more efficient operations per ton transported.
Supports choices that reduce low-efficiency displacement.
Makes estimation limits explicit before communicating impact.
regional: Helps plan operations in Amazon corridors with seasonality and limited connectivity.
Supports cooperatives and local operators with predictability.
Adds regional context without absolute promises.
automation: Organizes terms and documents before contracting.
Avoids delays by making pending items explicit in the flow.
Creates a simple trail for auditing and support.
brdomar: Clarifies the institutional guidelines around cabotage in Brazil.
Avoids mixing public policy context with product promises.
Supports plain-language communication for non-expert users.
compliance: Makes required and conditional requirements visible before shipment.
Reduces the risk of contracting without essential documents.
Facilitates auditing and coordination among parties.
connectivity: Supports recording evidence and events in low-signal segments.
Helps preserve traceability when syncing happens later.
Supports operations in communities and smaller terminals.
government: Helps visualize corridor indicators and document risk.
Supports enforcement and territorial coordination priorities.
Maintains separation between aggregated and private data.

cost: Demo indicator: may vary by route, cargo, utilization, and operational conditions.
It does not represent real cost without consolidated operational data.
sustainability: Demo indicator: depends on the replaced mode, distance, utilization, and river seasonality.
There is no single universal CO₂ percentage for all routes.
regional: Demo indicator: routes and volumes may vary by seasonality and local infrastructure.
It does not imply full coverage of the North Region.
automation: Demo indicator: depends on which documents and steps are in scope.
It does not equal automatic compliance with public agencies.
brdomar: Institutional context: it does not imply partnership, certification, or a running government program inside the product.
This indicator describes conceptual alignment, not regulatory compliance.
compliance: Demo indicator: document status does not replace official validation.
External integrations may require a dedicated implementation phase.
connectivity: Product hypothesis: behavior depends on real sync and local storage implementation.
Do not claim full offline operation if it is not implemented.
government: Demo indicator: data here is aggregated and does not replace official bases.
Avoid inferring real environmental status without a specific source.

cost: Consolidation of less-than-load cargoes on inland waterway routes.
Higher vessel utilization and fewer empty backhauls.
Comparable proposals and an auditable price history.
sustainability: Cabotage and inland waterways can be more efficient per ton in many scenarios; real gains depend on the route.
Visual indicators treat emission potential as a demo scenario, not field measurement.
Encourages comparing operators and routes before communicating environmental impact.
regional: Pilot routes among Belém, Santarém, Manaus, and Porto Velho.
Focus on cooperatives, small producers, and local operators.
automation: Quote, counteroffer, and acceptance in one digital line.
Documents and proofs attached to the negotiation.
brdomar: Alignment with Law No. 14.301/2022 and incentives for cabotage.
Integration with Brazilian ports and other modes.
Reduced reliance on road haulage and theft risk.
compliance: Tax, environmental, and sanitary documents are no longer a generic checklist.
Required, conditional, and next-phase states reduce contracting risk.
The mock trail prepares the app for real integrations with agencies and systems.
connectivity: The app acknowledges that not every stretch has stable signal.
Events can be recorded as operational evidence and synced later.
This creates a realistic narrative for communities and smaller terminals.
government: Corridor dashboards show supply, bioeconomy, risk, and documentation.
Territorial reading helps prioritize public policy and enforcement.

qaHub.sectionLead: Cards for testing on mock data. “Simulate user on login” fills the form (normal flow with OTP). “Sign in as this user” calls POST /api/mock-mode/login-as and redirects (no OTP). Visible only outside production or with a CI flag.
qaHub.feedbackError: Could not sign in as this fake user. Use dev/mock; in production only with a CI flag. Also check that the userId exists in the mock dataset.

tiala.represents: Approved shipper from Cooperativa Açaí Norte.
tiala.testsWhat: Publishing and managing own cargoes; shipper flows with an approved account.
tiala.validateLine: Validate that private routes load and cargoes tied to the owner appear.
tiala.expectedLine: Expected: full shipper experience without moderation blocks.
tiala.assistantNote: Cargo Status Assistant: use a cargo where you are the owner (e.g. marketplace scenario). Expected: card with summary, next steps, risks, and mock-ai source when applicable.
tiala.feedbackSuccess: You signed in as Tiala Rocha, approved shipper. Now test your own cargoes and the Cargo Status Assistant.

joao.testsWhat: Proposals and negotiations where the carrier is linked to the cargo.
joao.validateLine: Validate negotiation lists and access to linked cargoes.
joao.expectedLine: Expected: active carrier without moderation lock.
joao.assistantNote: Cargo Status Assistant: test a cargo that has a negotiation with this carrierId. Expected: assistant allowed; on cargo without link, blocked.
joao.feedbackSuccess: You signed in as João Navegante, approved carrier. Test linked negotiations and the assistant where in scope.

carlos.testsWhat: Compare authorized vs blocked access depending on negotiation/cargo chosen.
carlos.validateLine: On cargo without link to Carlos, expect block; with link, access.
carlos.expectedLine: Expected: stronger assistant and API scope control.
carlos.assistantNote: Use to validate blocking on others’ cargo: no sensitive data or authorized assistant out of scope.
carlos.feedbackSuccess: You signed in as Carlos (Hidrovias Madeira). Compare cargoes with and without a linked negotiation.

ana.testsWhat: Flows where a pending carrier hits restrictions (e.g. assistant, private areas).
ana.validateLine: Validate blocking messages or pending profile per current UI.
ana.expectedLine: Expected: blocks for approved=false where the product applies.
ana.assistantNote: Cargo Status Assistant: with Ana signed in, expect block for unapproved account before cargo scope.
ana.feedbackSuccess: You signed in as Ana RiosLog (moderation). Validate pending-carrier restrictions.

admin.testsWhat: Admin panel, mock scenario switching, and restricted tools.
admin.validateLine: Validate authorization to /admin route and mock-mode POST when applicable.
admin.expectedLine: Expected: full control over demo datasets.
admin.assistantNote: Admin bypasses assistant scope — useful for quick smoke on any cargo.
admin.feedbackSuccess: You signed in as administrator. Use mock mode and broad validations.
